These pages are practical references for computational methods I use regularly. They are organized as cookbooks: concrete algorithms, working code, and guidance on when and how to use each technique. The emphasis is on getting correct results with reliable error estimates.

For the underlying physics and mathematical context, see the corresponding [Notes & Expositions](../notes/index.qmd).

---

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### [Julia Tensor Network Workflows](julia-tensor-networks.qmd) {.unnumbered}
Setting up ITensor.jl, building Hamiltonians, running DMRG, and measuring observables. A practical guide to tensor network calculations in Julia.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### [Monte Carlo Error Analysis](monte-carlo-errors.qmd) {.unnumbered}
Bootstrap, jackknife, and blocking methods for estimating statistical errors in Monte Carlo data. Implementations in Python and Julia.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon=false}
### [Data Analysis for Monte Carlo](data-analysis.qmd) {.unnumbered}
Autocorrelation estimation, binning analysis, and the practical workflow from raw simulation data to publication-quality error bars.
:::
